    67	## Proof Strategy
    68	
    69	Use disagreement edges for binary time evolution, injective threshold
    70	encoding for median evolution, an explicit small counting obstruction to
    71	independent inverse layers, and edgewise conjugation for orientations.
    72	No general majority-network convergence theorem, statistical experiment,
    73	or unread source theorem is required for these deductions.
    74	
    75	## Dependency Map
    76	
    77	1. The binary update identity in Step 1 gives zero persistence and
    78	   erosion of disagreement runs.
    79	2. Run erosion and the cyclic parity constraint give every recurrent
    80	   state, exact depth and sharp witnesses.
    81	3. The threshold/median equivalence gives the finite-chain assertions.
    82	4. The three-site example disproves the independent inverse-product claim.
    83	5. Reversal interchanges sources and sinks, giving C.
    84	6. The complete generic ring-preimage proof read in fresh12 is used only
    85	   in the subtraction discussion, not as a new theorem.

    87	## Proof
    88	
    89	### Step 1. Binary majority acts by eroding disagreement runs
    90	
    91	A bit changes exactly when both neighbors differ from it. Hence
    92	$$
    93	(Mx)_i=x_i\oplus(d_{i-1}d_i).
    94	$$
    95	Subtracting the two neighboring new bits gives
    96	$$
    97	d'_i=d_i\oplus d_{i-1}d_i\oplus d_id_{i+1}
    98	=d_i(1\oplus d_{i-1}\oplus d_{i+1}).
    99	$$
   100	In particular, a zero disagreement edge stays zero. If the word $d$ has
   101	at least one zero, its maximal one-runs remain separated forever.
   102	
   103	A run of length one has zeros on both sides, so its sole one survives.
   104	In a run of length at least two, each endpoint sees one neighboring zero
   105	and one neighboring one and disappears; every interior one sees two
   106	neighboring ones and survives. A length-two run disappears completely.
   107	Thus each even run of length $2k$ vanishes after exactly $k$ steps, while
   108	each odd run of length $2k+1$ becomes a singleton after exactly $k$ steps.
   109	
   110	### Step 2. Recurrence, exact clock and sharpness
   111	
   112	The binary word is fixed exactly when $d_{i-1}d_i=0$ at every site.
   113	For $d\neq1^n$, Step 1 therefore gives
   114	$$
   115	\operatorname{depth}(x)=\lfloor L(d)/2\rfloor.
   116	$$
   117	For strictness, at every earlier time a maximal run still has length at
   118	least two, so some site changes. It cannot already be periodic: the number
   119	of disagreement edges strictly decreases whenever such a run exists.
   120	When no such run remains, the word is fixed.
   121	
   122	If $d=1^n$, cyclic parity
   123	$$
   124	\bigoplus_{i=0}^{n-1}d_i=0
   125	$$
   126	forces $n$ even. The two possible binary words alternate and each site
   127	changes at every step, giving exact period two. There is no other
   128	nonfixed recurrent state by the preceding strict-decrease argument.
   129	
   130	For every nonalternating word, $L(d)\leq n-1$, giving the global bound.
   131	For $n=2k+1\geq3$, choose $d=1^{2k}0$; for $n=2k+2\geq4$, choose
   132	$d=1^{2k}00$. Each has an even number of ones and hence lifts to a
   133	cyclic binary word: choose $x_0=0$ and recursively set
   134	$x_{i+1}=x_i\oplus d_i$, with cyclic closure supplied by that parity.
   135	Its depth is $k=\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$.
   136	
   137	At $n=1$, the three entries of the local rule are the same bit and all
   138	states are fixed. At $n=2$, the two neighbor entries are the other bit,
   139	so $M(x_0,x_1)=(x_1,x_0)$; all states are periodic and have depth zero.
   140	These agree with the stated formula.
   141	
   142	### Step 3. Ordered median layers are a coupled lift
   143	
   144	For any three ordered values and every threshold $a$, their median is at
   145	least $a$ if and only if at least two of those values are at least $a$.
   146	Consequently
   147	$$
   148	\theta_a(\mathcal M_qx)=M(\theta_a(x)).
   149	$$
   150	The entire threshold tuple is injective, since
   151	$$
   152	x_i=\sum_{a=1}^{q-1}\theta_a(x)_i.
   153	$$
   154	Its layers are nested:
   155	$\theta_{a+1}(x)_i\leq\theta_a(x)_i$ for every $a,i$.
   156	
   157	If a finite-chain state is periodic, every threshold layer is periodic.
   158	Conversely, if every layer is periodic, Step 2 says all its layer periods
   159	divide two, so injectivity gives $\mathcal M_q^2x=x$.
   160	Applying this statement along the orbit proves
   161	$$
   162	\operatorname{depth}(x)=
   163	\max_{1\leq a\leq q-1}\operatorname{depth}(\theta_a(x)).
   164	$$
   165	The binary result supplies the upper bound. Embedding a sharp binary word
   166	using the two values $0$ and $q-1$ supplies equality, including $n=1,2$.
   167	This is threshold transport of the binary clock, not a new mechanism
   168	created by enlarging the alphabet.
   169	
   170	### Step 4. Independent inverse layers overcount
   171	
   172	Take $n=q=3$ and the finite-chain target $y=(1,1,1)$.
   173	Each three-point neighborhood is the entire three-site ring.
   174	Its threshold targets are $111$ and $000$. Under binary majority, each
   175	has four predecessors, which would give $16$ independent layer pairs.
   176	
   177	The actual finite-chain fibre has size $13$. Among all $27$ ternary
   178	words, the output median is zero exactly when at least two entries are
   179	zero, giving $1+3\cdot2=7$ words. Median two gives another disjoint
   180	seven. The remaining $27-7-7=13$ have median one.
   181	
   182	An explicit inadmissible layer pair is
   183	$\theta_1=110$, $\theta_2=001$: it has the required binary outputs but
   184	violates $\theta_2\leq\theta_1$ at the last coordinate. Thus the
   185	independent product is not a valid full-target inverse formula.
   186	These counts follow by finite case partition on paper; no pilot executed.

   188	### Step 5. Source/sink convention changes do not create a new map

   190	Reversal $R$ is an involution on the finite set of acyclic orientations.
   191	The sources of $R(O)$ are exactly the sinks of $O$.
   192	Reversal of all edges commutes with reversal of any specified edge set.
   193	Therefore, edge by edge,

   195	F_{\rm src}=R\circ F_{\rm snk}\circ R.

   198	The acyclic carrier is preserved: after a source is flipped it is a sink,
